articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.12373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in strategic and advisory contexts, yet their safety alignment is typically evaluated in English only. Conventional width or depth scaling increases both costs together because every added layer is evaluated in both phases. articles.summary: Dual-Flow Transformers decouple prefill and decode computation paths to optimize hardware utilization for different inference bottlenecks.

articles.summary: PAC-Bayes-regularized Meta-LoRA enables cross-domain few-shot personalization of LLMs by calibrating adaptation magnitude through meta-learning.

articles.summary: Governed Persistent Memory (GPM) provides an auditable bitemporal state model for long-horizon agents with source-bound admission and fail-closed release.

articles.summary: Researchers introduce trie automata, a specialized constrained decoding mechanism that efficiently handles LLM output generation from large finite sets by exploiting shared prefixes and structure, overcoming performance limitations of general-purpose grammar compilation at scale.

articles.summary: NL2SHACL-Bench introduces a benchmark suite for evaluating natural language to SHACL shape translation, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation methods for this knowledge graph validation task.

articles.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern agentic AI systems combine multiple large language model agents with heterogeneous skills, yet most architectures either fix communication in advance or allow full broadcast. articles.summary: A cooperative game-theoretic approach to optimize communication and coalition formation among heterogeneous LLM agents, balancing token costs and latency in multi-agent systems.

articles.title: MetaSpace: Metamorphic Testing for Spatial Cognition in Embodied Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An embodied agent is an intelligent entity that interacts with its environment through a physical body. articles.summary: MetaSpace proposes metamorphic testing methods to evaluate spatial cognition in embodied agents, moving beyond task completion metrics to uncover critical vulnerabilities and safety violations.

articles.title: TREAT: Evaluating Access to Formal Knowledge across Equivalent Mathematical Representations
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly operate between flexible input representations and formal objects used by downstream tools. A key challenge is recognizing when an unfamiliar formulation denotes a known formal object. articles.summary: TREAT benchmark evaluates whether LLMs can recognize equivalent mathematical theorems across different formal representations, testing access to formal knowledge.

articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous research loops driven by large language models can run machine-learning experiments at scale but tend to drift toward local refinements of whichever metric they optimise rather than testing the hypotheses that motivate the experiments. articles.summary: An autonomous research loop driven by LLMs for quadruped robot navigation adds structural components to prevent metric drift and ensure falsifiable hypothesis testing.

articles.title: TeXFix-Bench: An Empirically Grounded Multi-Format Benchmark for LLM-Based Document Source Repair
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific and technical writing depends on markup sources that must compile: LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown pipelines fail on missing delimiters, mismatched environments, broken imports, or package conflicts. articles.summary: TeXFix-Bench provides a multi-format benchmark for evaluating LLM-based document repair across LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown, grounded in empirically mined fault models.

articles.title: CMU-Drive and V2V-VLA: Cooperative Multi-agent Unified Driving with Reasoning Benchmark and Vehicle-to-Vehicle Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently achieved impressive performance for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet existing approaches are primarily designed for an individual single autonomous driving agent with limited support for cooperative perception, reasoning, and planning. articles.summary: CMU-Drive introduces a closed-loop benchmark for cooperative autonomous driving with vision-language-action models, enabling multi-agent reasoning and perception in safety-critical scenarios.

articles.title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory enables AI agents to maintain continuity across sessions, personalize behavior, and evolve through accumulated experience. Yet memory evolution is not simply a process of storing more information: new experiences may reinforce, revise, or interfere with existing memory states. articles.summary: Controlled Memory Interference framework addresses long-term memory management in continual LLM agents, enabling agents to navigate conflicting or temporally-sensitive memories.

articles.title: Contextual Value Alignment via Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values remains a major challenge, especially for trustworthy AI. articles.title: Mendel G\"odel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improving coding agents that iteratively rewrite their own source code have demonstrated impressive performance on coding tasks. articles.summary: Mendel Gödel Machine introduces comparative evolution-based self-modification for coding agents, enabling them to iteratively improve by learning from archives of past attempts rather than single failures.
